summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and hypercholesterolemia was admitted for left-sided chest pain radiating to the arm and leg, which woke her at 3 a.m. The pain was similar to prior episodes previously determined to be non-cardiac. Serial troponins were negative, EKGs showed no changes, and a chest X-ray revealed no acute abnormalities, ruling out acute cardiac or pulmonary causes. Her symptoms were attributed to likely musculoskeletal, neuropathic, or gastrointestinal origins. She presented with hyperglycemia (blood glucose 500), managed by adjusting her insulin regimen to 60 units glargine at bedtime and 20 units lispro with meals, plus sliding scale. She was restarted on omeprazole after clarification that her insurance covers it and advised to resume daily aspirin. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged and clear instructions for medication adjustments, blood sugar monitoring, and when to seek care.
